1 ## Sealed comparison (U57, U58) 2 - Purpose: compare several published arms on one box under a design fixed before the run. Owner approval 2026-11-03 (contract gaps G1 comparison arms, G3 tolerance and equivalence, G6 compute metadata of the blind-02 science route); requirements from science steps s13 to s23. Arms are published programs or configurations that need no new code, run by the pipeline from sealed argument vectors. Each invocation runs one arm on one input, and invocations are interleaved on one box. No agent computes a number: every number comes from the pipeline's trusted wall time, from rules fixed before the run and applied by the pipeline, from a trusted comparator of two arms' outputs, or from a published evaluator that runs on each arm's output without access to the arm's identity. Criteria, margins, thresholds, reference values and timeouts are fixed by a science step before the run, sealed, and unreadable by the run's agents and by the processes of arms and evaluator. Compute is recorded twice and never mixed: per invocation as attribution and per box allocation as the bill. Never change a criterion after a result: every decision uses the sealed design. An outcome that is not supported is a result and never fails a stage. Comparisons that need more than one run are split by the science step into one design per run; a design whose launch depends on an earlier run's outcomes is launched only when the science step finds them in that run's `C/comparison_scored.json`. Without `args.comparison`, every stage is unchanged. Declared residual risks, which no rule below removes: the evaluator reads the arm's output files by design, so file names or content under `out/` that identify the program can reach it (the sealed `evaluate.sh` bytes make any dependence on them auditable after the run); state of shared hardware (device memory, caches, timing) is not cleared between parts; and a harness script that disobeys the rule that only `fetch_private.sh` handles the evaluator's private data can leave a transformed copy of them (an archive, a re-encoding, a derived file) where the arm part can read it, which the byte-identity check of Separated users step 7 does not detect (`setup.sh` and its repairs are kept in `A/harness/` and the stage's receipts, so such a copy is auditable after the run). 3 - Optional `args.comparison` is an object with exactly the key `design`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a design JSON file. It is exclusive with `args.card`, `args.units_check` and `args.units_probe`. The design is exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, evaluator, replicates, warmup, order_seed, timeout_s, budget_s, bootstrap_seed, bootstrap_resamples, comparisons}`: 4 - `arms`: 2 to 5 items, each exactly `{id, what, commands, env}`; ids `"A0"`, `"A1"`, ... in order; `what` a non-empty string. `A0` is the published baseline that intake and reproduce handle as usual. 5 - `commands`: 1 to 8 commands, each a non-empty array of non-empty strings: the exact published command lines of the arm, in order, as argument vectors run without a shell. The pipeline runs them (see Evaluate); the arm's adapter only prepares. 6 - `env`: null or an object mapping names that match `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$` and do not start with `CMP_` to strings; set for the arm's commands. 7 - Placeholders, in command and `env` strings only: `{input}` (the input id), `{run}`, `{out}` (the absolute paths of the invocation's `run/` and `out/`) and `{spec:

}` with `

` a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the input's `spec`, which must resolve in every input's `spec` to a string (inserted as is) or a finite number (inserted as `json.dumps` writes it). `{{` and `}}` stand for literal braces; any other `{` or `}` makes the design invalid. Substitution replaces every occurrence and is not repeated on its result. 8 - `inputs`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{id, spec}`: `id` a unique string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`; `spec` any JSON value (pins, case, configuration). 9 - `outputs`: 0 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, what, format, select}`: a logical result each arm, or the evaluator, writes for an input, compared across arms. `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `what` a non-empty string; `format` `"bytes"`, `"text_numbers"` (every number in the file's UTF-8 text, in order, as matched by `[-+]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][-+]?\d+)?` together with `nan`, `inf` and `-inf` tokens) or `"json_numbers"` (every number leaf of the JSON document, in document order; booleans are not numbers). `select` is null (the whole content) or, for `bytes` and `text_numbers` only, a Python `re` pattern with at least one capturing group: the content is read as UTF-8 with replacement, and the selected content is every group of every match of `re.finditer(select, text, re.MULTILINE)`, in order (an unmatched group as the empty string), joined by `"\n"`; `format` then applies to the selected content (`bytes` to its UTF-8 encoding). Several outputs may select different parts of the same file, each with its own comparison and tolerance. 10 - `metrics`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, unit, what, source, reduce, expect_count}`: `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `unit` and `what` non-empty strings; `source` `"trusted_wall"` or `"sealed_extraction"`. 11 - `trusted_wall`: the invocation's wall seconds: the adapter's wall plus its commands' walls, plus the evaluator's wall when the design has an evaluator. `reduce` and `expect_count` are null. 12 - `sealed_extraction`: read from fetched files by a rule the harness agent fixes before the run, reduced as the design states. `reduce` `"first"`, `"max"` or `"value_at_max_key"`; `expect_count` null or a positive integer, the number of matched values the rule must find. 13 - `evaluator`: null or exactly `{what, spec, timeout_s}`: a published, pinned program that reads one arm's output for one input, with data that only it may read, and writes evaluation files. `what` a non-empty string; `spec` any JSON value (program, pin, command, and where its private data come from); `timeout_s` null or a positive integer. 14 - `replicates` an integer from 1 to 30; `warmup` an integer from 0 to 3; `order_seed` and `bootstrap_seed` integers; `bootstrap_resamples` an integer from 1000 to 1000000; `budget_s` a positive integer, the evaluate stage's time budget for this comparison. When `args.run_ceiling_s` is present, `budget_s` must be below it. 15 - `timeout_s`: null, a positive integer for every invocation, or an object mapping every arm id to a positive integer or to an object mapping every input id to a positive integer: the cap of one invocation's arm part. 16 - `comparisons`: 0 to 12 items (0: a run that only records values and compute, for example to derive later reference values), each exactly `{id, arm, against, measure, criterion, direction, unit, pairing, rule, confidence, margin, threshold, strict, reference, missing, given, parts}`: 17 - `id` unique, matching `^K[0-9]{1,2}$`; `arm` an arm id; `against` a different arm id or `"reference"`; `parts` a non-empty array of unique non-empty strings. 18 - `measure` is exactly `{metric}` (a metric name) or exactly `{output, comparator}` (an output name and one of `"exact"`, `"elementwise_abs"`, `"elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max"`). An output comparison needs an arm as `against`. 19 - `criterion` `"agreement"` (every output comparison and no metric comparison), `"non_inferiority"`, `"superiority"` or `"ratio_at_least"`. 20 - `direction` `"higher_better"`, `"lower_better"` or `"two_sided"`: the metric as measured (for wall seconds, `lower_better`). `agreement` and `superiority` use `two_sided`; `non_inferiority` and `ratio_at_least` use `higher_better` or `lower_better`. 21 - `unit` `"pooled_mean"` (each replicate's value is the mean over inputs, decided once), `"per_input_all"` (decided per input; the comparison holds only if it holds on every input) or `"per_input_each"` (decided and reported per input). 22 - `pairing` `"paired_replicate"` or `"unpaired"`; `rule` `"all_pairs"` or `"bootstrap"`; `confidence` a number in `[0.5, 1)` for `bootstrap` and null for `all_pairs`. `ratio_at_least` uses exactly `pooled_mean`, `paired_replicate` and `bootstrap`; every other criterion uses `all_pairs` and a per-input unit; agreement uses `paired_replicate`. 23 - `margin`: for an output comparison, the comparator's tolerance: null for `exact`, `{"abs": x}` for `elementwise_abs`, `{"abs": x, "rel": y}` for `elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max`. For `non_inferiority` and `superiority`, null or `{"abs": x}`. For `ratio_at_least`, null. `x` and `y` are finite and nonnegative. 24 - `threshold`: a finite number above 0 for `ratio_at_least`, otherwise null. `strict`: a boolean for `ratio_at_least` (true: the bound must exceed `threshold`; false: it may equal it), otherwise null. 25 - `reference`: exactly when `against` is `"reference"`, an object `{source, values}`: `source` a non-empty string naming where the values come from (for example an earlier run of this route and the rule that derived them), `values` mapping every input id to a finite number; otherwise null. A reference needs a metric `measure`, a per-input unit and `unpaired`. 26 - `missing`: `"void"` or `"fail"`, how a missing value is decided (see Scoring). 27 - `given`: an array, possibly empty, of unique ids of comparisons that come earlier in `comparisons`; a decision unit is decided only when each of them is supported for it (see Scoring). 28 An invalid argument or design, or a path that cannot be read as JSON, fails intake with `error_class: parse` before any agent call. 29 - Before the intake agent call and any box command, the pipeline writes atomically, in this order: `C/comparison.json`, exactly `{source, source_sha256, design}`; `C/comparison_seal.json`, exactly `{comparison_sha256, sealed_utc}` (the SHA-256 of the exact bytes of `C/comparison.json`); and `A/comparison_view.json`, exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, evaluator, replicates, warmup}` copied from the design, with `evaluator` reduced to `{what, spec}` (null when the design's is null). The view holds no comparison, criterion, margin, threshold, reference value, timeout, part, seed or budget. Agents see only the view; comparison-mode prompts name it and never `C/` or the design path. The science step that writes the design is responsible for the view's free text (`what`, `spec`, `select`) stating no expectation, criterion or result, and for keeping no copy of the design on the pipeline host outside the paths hidden below. 30 - Isolation of agent calls, comparison mode only. Every agent call of the run (intake, harness, and every setup and anchors repair) is dispatched with wf `isolation` (see Implement) as implement's calls are: `directory` a fresh private view created for that call under the system temporary directory, `box_access` false, and `hidden` holding the run root, the workflow journal directory, the design file's parent directory and, when the design file lies inside a git work tree, that work tree's top-level directory (the nearest ancestor that contains `.git`). A missing or invalid `wrap.json` or fetched file is not invalid input; it is a missing value. Diagnostics contain no input content. A scoring failure fails evaluate with `error_class: parse`. 88 - Evaluate status in comparison mode is PASS once `C/comparison_scored.json` was written, whatever the outcomes. ## Sealed comparison (U57, U58) - Purpose: compare several published arms on one box under a design fixed before the run. Owner approval 2026-11-03 (contract gaps G1 comparison arms, G3 tolerance and equivalence, G6 compute metadata of the blind-02 science route); requirements from science steps s13 to s23. Arms are published programs or configurations that need no new code, run by the pipeline from sealed argument vectors. Each invocation runs one arm on one input, and invocations are interleaved on one box. No agent computes a number: every number comes from the pipeline's trusted wall time, from rules fixed before the run and applied by the pipeline, from a trusted comparator of two arms' outputs, or from a published evaluator that runs on each arm's output without access to the arm's identity. Criteria, margins, thresholds, reference values and timeouts are fixed by a science step before the run, sealed, and unreadable by the run's agents and by the processes of arms and evaluator. Compute is recorded twice and never mixed: per invocation as attribution and per box allocation as the bill. Never change a criterion after a result: every decision uses the sealed design. An outcome that is not supported is a result and never fails a stage. Comparisons that need more than one run are split by the science step into one design per run; a design whose launch depends on an earlier run's outcomes is launched only when the science step finds them in that run's `C/comparison_scored.json`. Without `args.comparison`, every stage is unchanged. Declared residual risks, which no rule below removes: the evaluator reads the arm's output files by design, so file names or content under `out/` that identify the program can reach it (the sealed `evaluate.sh` bytes make any dependence on them auditable after the run); state of shared hardware (device memory, caches, timing) is not cleared between parts; and a harness script that disobeys the rule that only `fetch_private.sh` handles the evaluator's private data can leave a transformed copy of them (an archive, a re-encoding, a derived file) where the arm part can read it, which the byte-identity check of Separated users step 7 does not detect (`setup.sh` and its repairs are kept in `A/harness/` and the stage's receipts, so such a copy is auditable after the run). - Optional `args.comparison` is an object with exactly the key `design`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a design JSON file. A side of an (input, replicate) pair is missing when its invocation's status is not `ok`, when the location is under `eval` and `eval_status` is not `ok`, when the location names no file or an unreadable one, when the content cannot be parsed as the output's `format`, or when the selected content is empty (no bytes for `bytes`, no numbers otherwise). - Output comparisons (`agreement`): for each input and replicate where neither side is missing, the comparator compares the two contents. `exact`: identical bytes. Otherwise both contents are parsed as the output's `format` into number lists; different lengths, or a NaN in one list but not at the same position in the other, disagree; equal infinities agree; finite pairs agree when `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol` (`elementwise_abs`) or `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol + rel_tol * max(abs(a), abs(b))` (`elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max`). A pair agrees when every element agrees. Each compared pair records `max_abs_error` and `max_rel_error` over its finite elements (null when none). - Metric comparisons: an arm's value for (replicate, input) is the metric value above. For `pooled_mean`, a replicate's value is the mean over inputs, null when any input's value is null. Per decision unit (the pooled value, or each input): for `paired_replicate`, the differences are `arm - against` per replicate; for `unpaired`, the differences of every arm value with every against value, or of every arm value with the input's reference value. `ratio_at_least` uses the ratio of means `mean(arm) / mean(against)` for `higher_better` and `mean(against) / mean(arm)` for `lower_better`. - Missing values, per decision unit: `n_missing` counts the arm's missing values and, against an arm, the against arm's (for `pooled_mean` a replicate counts once; for agreement a pair with a missing side counts once). With `"void"`, any missing value makes the unit void with reason `"missing_values"`. With `"fail"`, a missing value of `arm` makes the unit `"not_supported"` with reason `"missing_values"`, and otherwise a missing value of `against` makes it void with reason `"missing_values"`. - Eligibility (`given`): for each listed comparison, its outcome for this unit is that comparison's row for the same input when both comparisons are decided per input, and otherwise that comparison's outcome, where `"per_input"` counts as supported only when every row is. When any of these is not `"supported"`, the unit is void with reason `"not_eligible"`. - Interval: for `all_pairs`, `[lo, hi]` is the minimum and maximum of the differences, and needs at least one difference. For `bootstrap`, the ratio of means is recomputed on `bootstrap_resamples` resamples (`B`) with replacement of the unit's paired replicates, drawn from one `random.Random(bootstrap_seed)` stream in comparison order, and `[lo, hi]` is the `(1 - confidence) / 2` and `(1 + confidence) / 2` empirical quantiles (sorted resamples, index `floor(q * (B - 1))`); it needs at least two replicates. `estimate` is the mean difference (`all_pairs`) or the ratio of means (`bootstrap`) on the full data. Too few values gives outcome `"void"` with reason `"insufficient_replicates"`. - Margin value `m`: 0 for a null margin, `x` for `{"abs": x}`. - Outcome per decision unit, in this order: eligibility; then, for agreement, any compared pair that disagrees makes the unit not supported; then the missing-value rule; then the interval's minimum count; then the criterion. The criterion gives `"supported"`, `"not_supported"` or else `"inconclusive"`: agreement is supported when at least one pair was compared, every compared pair agrees and none is missing (with no compared pair, it is void with reason `"missing_values"`); non-inferiority (`higher_better`) is supported when `lo >= -m`, not supported when `hi < -m`; non-inferiority (`lower_better`) is supported when `hi <= m`, not supported when `lo > m`; superiority (`two_sided`) is supported when `lo > m` or `hi < -m`, not supported when `-m <= lo` and `hi <= m`; ratio with `strict` false is supported when `lo >= threshold`, not supported when `hi < threshold`; ratio with `strict` true is supported when `lo > threshold`, not supported when `hi <= threshold`. - `sign` of a unit is `"higher"` when a superiority is supported with `lo > m`, `"lower"` when it is supported with `hi < -m`, and null otherwise. - A comparison's outcome: for `pooled_mean`, its one unit's outcome; for `per_input_all`, supported when every input is supported, not supported when any input is not supported, void when any input is void and none is not supported, otherwise inconclusive; for `per_input_each`, `"per_input"`, with each input's outcome in its rows. - `C/comparison_scored.json`, atomic, is exactly `{comparison_sha256, comparisons, totals}`. `comparisons` follows the design's order, each exactly `{id, arm, against, criterion, unit, outcome, rows}`; `rows` has one row per decision unit (`input` null for `pooled_mean`), each exactly `{input, n, n_missing, estimate, lo, hi, margin_value, threshold, outcome, sign, reason, pairs}`. `n` counts the differences, ratios or compared pairs; `pairs` is null for metric comparisons and, for agreement, the per-replicate rows `{replicate, agrees, missing, max_abs_error, max_rel_error}` (`agrees` null and `missing` true when a side is missing). Numbers are null when void; `reason` is `"missing_values"`, `"insufficient_replicates"` or `"not_eligible"` for a void unit, `"missing_values"` for a unit made not supported by the `"fail"` rule, and null otherwise. `totals` is exactly `{supported, not_supported, inconclusive, void}`, counting decision units over all comparisons. - Exit 0 after writing; exit 1 for invalid or missing input, a seal mismatch or a failed write, with no output file. A missing or invalid `wrap.json` or fetched file is not invalid input; it is a missing value. Diagnostics contain no input content. A scoring failure fails evaluate with `error_class: parse`. - Evaluate status in comparison mode is PASS once `C/comparison_scored.json` was written, whatever the outcomes. Evaluate facts keep every existing key, null in comparison mode.
